_doc: Submodules whose gitlink advance is EXPECTED to be refused, with the reason.
A refusal is normally a real finding and must fail. But a STANDING refusal that
cannot be resolved from here turns advance-submodule-pointers permanently red,
and a workflow that has been red for weeks is one nobody reads — which is how a
genuinely NEW refusal (an app whose development was force-pushed, say) arrives
looking exactly like the old one.
An entry here is reported and does NOT fail. Anything not here still fails.
An entry that has STOPPED being refused also fails, so a dead entry cannot sit
here silently pre-authorising the next divergence in that app.
EVERY ENTRY REQUIRES FOUR FIELDS (2026-09-03 ratchet): app, reason,
first_seen (YYYY-MM-DD — the date the refusal was first observed), and
review_condition (the human-readable condition under which it should be
removed). An entry missing any of the four is not an entry — it is dropped
and its app fails like any unlisted refusal. An entry whose first_seen is
more than 7 days before the run EXPIRES on its own: it stops suppressing the
failure with no human action, so a standing waiver cannot silently outlive
the week the design gives someone to act on review_condition. See
loadAllowedRefusals() and REFUSAL_MAX_AGE_DAYS in advance-submodule-pointers.mjs.

2026-08-28: the R80.4 entry was removed. Its stated review condition - "when R80.4's ruleset allows a merge commit, or its development is recreated from main" - was met: R80.4 was reconciled with a merge commit (R80.4#266), so the app is no longer refused. The gate itself demanded the removal, which is the entry's own design: a dead entry must not sit here pre-authorising the next divergence.
2026-09-03: the predicate itself was fixed to compare each app's gitlink
against that app's MAIN tip rather than its DEVELOPMENT head (a development-
main promotion merge diverges those two branches from each other by
construction, which is what was refusing conduit/R80.4/throughput — none of
them for a real defect). Measured locally against this fix on 2026-09-03:
conduit, R80.4 and throughput all read as ALREADY CURRENT (their bsuite
gitlink already equals their own main tip), so no entries were needed for
them here. crm7 newly refuses instead — its bsuite development gitlink
(70aef71f) is crm7's own DEVELOPMENT tip, not main, so it now sits AHEAD of
crm7's main (1fd4fd82) and the forward-only rule correctly won't move it
backward. That is a real, unresolved finding (see bsuite#2939's PR body,
which makes the same "both at main" claim and is false for crm7 specifically)
and is deliberately NOT allowlisted here — it needs a human decision, not a
waiver.
